nodes.body: Lila skipped along, her hand snug in Grandpa's warm one. Tied to her wrist with a floppy yellow bow bounced her favorite thing: a big red balloon, round and shiny as an apple. It tugged in the soft breeze, tap, tap, tap. "Look, ducks!" Lila giggled, skipping down the grassy path.

choices.label: Skip down the park path.

nodes.body: Whoosh! A big gust of breeze rushed by, and the floppy bow wiggled loose. The big red balloon slipped right off Lila's wrist and floated up, up, just past her reaching fingertips. "Oh!" she gasped. Grandpa squeezed her hand. "Quick," he said, "let's follow it!"

choices.label: Chase the big red balloon!

nodes.body: They trotted down the path after the big red balloon, red and round against the bright blue sky. It bounced along on the breeze, always just out of reach, drifting ahead of them toward the spot where the path split into two.

choices.label: Run to where the path splits.

nodes.body: At the fork, the balloon hung in the air as if it were choosing too. Down to the left, the path sloped toward the shiny duck pond, smooth and easy. Up to the right, it climbed toward the open sky and grassy kite hill. The breeze tugged the balloon high that way.

choices.label: Follow it down to the shiny duck pond.
Follow it up grassy kite hill.

nodes.body: Down by the shiny duck pond, the big red balloon skimmed low over the cool water, its string trailing behind like a little tail. A row of fluffy ducks paddled after it in a bumpy line, splashing softly. It drifted toward the reeds by the old willow tree.

choices.label: Hurry around the shiny duck pond.

nodes.body: Lila and Grandpa hurried along the muddy bank while the line of ducks paddled beside them, feathers fluffed, splashing softly. Up ahead, the string caught, quiet and still, in the tall green reeds by the old willow tree.

choices.label: Go to the reeds by the old willow tree.

nodes.body: The big red balloon bobbed above the reeds, its string tangled just out of reach over the water. Flat, smooth stepping stones led out toward the old willow tree. Nearby, the paddle-boat lady waved from her little wooden boat. "Which way, Lila?" asked Grandpa.

choices.label: Tiptoe across flat stepping stones.
Wave to the paddle-boat lady.

nodes.body: Holding tight to Grandpa's hand, Lila tiptoed from stone to stone, splish, steady, splish. The ducks watched quietly, like a little audience. At the last stone, the big red balloon bobbed in the twigs of the old willow tree, right above her head.

choices.label: Stop under the old willow tree.

nodes.body: The balloon's string was looped loosely around a bendy twig, just a little too high to reach. Grandpa spotted a long, smooth stick by the bank. A puffing breeze kept rustling the willow's leaves. "Stick, or breeze?" he asked. "You choose, Lila."

choices.label: Reach up with a long smooth stick.
Wait for a puffing breeze to help.

nodes.body: Grandpa held Lila steady while she stretched the long, smooth stick way, way up. The tip nudged the loop of string, and slowly, slowly it slid down the twig, closer and closer to her open hand.

choices.label: Catch the string!

nodes.body: The string dropped right into Lila's hand. Got it! She wound it twice around her wrist, and Grandpa tied the bow extra tight. The ducks quacked a happy hooray, and the old willow tree rustled its leaves. Lila and Grandpa walked home, the big red balloon bouncing proudly beside them.

Lila and Grandpa sat still and quiet on the last stone to watch. The puffing breeze puffed once, twice, and the string slipped free of the twig. But instead of drifting down, the big red balloon floated gently out over the calm middle of the pond.

choices.label: Watch where it goes.

nodes.body: The big red balloon drifted down and landed softly on the calm, glassy water, round and red like a little boat. One by one, the fluffy ducks paddled over, circling it slowly, as if it were a brand new friend.

choices.label: Wave to the duck parade.

nodes.body: The ducks paddled in a proud circle around the big red balloon, quacking a happy song, while the littlest duckling bobbed beside it like a tiny guard. Lila giggled and waved from the stones. Her balloon had become the leader of the duck parade, and that felt like a very happy trade.

The paddle-boat lady glided her little wooden boat to the muddy bank and helped Lila and Grandpa climb aboard. Everyone held on snug. Out on the shiny duck pond, the big red balloon bobbed low over the water, its string dancing on the rippling waves.

choices.label: Pedal after the big red balloon.

nodes.body: They pedaled and pedaled, splish, splash, splish. The ducks raced alongside like a cheerful little escort. Up ahead, the big red balloon skipped along on the breeze, straight toward the big whooshing fountain.

choices.label: Follow it to the big whooshing fountain.

nodes.body: The big whooshing fountain sprayed a cool, silver mist, and the big red balloon bounced softly on top of it, boing, boing, like the fountain was juggling it. Then it rolled down the spray, sliding closer and closer to the little boat.

choices.label: Hold out both hands.

nodes.body: Plop! The big red balloon rolled right off the spray and landed in Lila's open arms, cool and misty. The paddle-boat lady cheered, and the ducks quacked hooray. They pedaled back to shore with the big red balloon riding proudly in Lila's lap like a round red captain.

Up grassy kite hill they climbed, puff, puff. The big red balloon climbed higher too, a round red dot against the white, fluffy clouds. Partway up, Lila heard a jingly bell on the hillside and saw the kite kids swooping and laughing at the top.

choices.label: Keep climbing toward the sounds.

nodes.body: The jingly bell came from the ice-cream cart with its tall striped umbrella, parked on the sunny hillside. Above it, the kite kids flew swooping, colorful kites at the very top. The big red balloon wobbled in between, unsure which way to go.

choices.label: See where the big red balloon goes.

nodes.body: The big red balloon dipped low toward the ice-cream cart's striped umbrella, then bobbed back up toward the kite kids at the windy top of the hill. It couldn't make up its mind. Grandpa squeezed Lila's hand. "You get to pick where we try to catch it," he said.

choices.label: Run to the ice-cream cart.
Climb up to the kite kids.

nodes.body: Just as they reached the ice-cream cart, the big red balloon bumped softly against the tall striped umbrella, and its string wrapped once around the wooden pole. The ice-cream man looked up from his scoops and smiled at his new balloon customer.

choices.label: Look up at the tangled string.

nodes.body: The string was wound tight around the pole, way up where the striped umbrella spread out, much too high for Lila. The ice-cream man was very tall, and he kept a little wooden step stool behind the cart. "Ask him, or climb the stool?" said Grandpa.

choices.label: Ask the ice-cream man to reach it.
Climb a little step stool and try.

nodes.body: The ice-cream man wiped his sticky hands, stood up on his tiptoes, and unwound the string, one loop, two loops. He caught the big red balloon before it could wiggle away, then bowed low like a fancy waiter.

choices.label: Take the big red balloon back.

nodes.body: The ice-cream man handed Lila the big red balloon as if it were the fanciest sundae on the whole menu, and added one small strawberry scoop for the brave balloon chaser. Lila tied the string tight, licked her cold, sweet ice cream, and grinned at Grandpa. What a delicious rescue.

Lila climbed the little wooden step stool while Grandpa held her steady. She stretched way up on her tiptoes, and her fingertips just brushed the very end of the dangling string. Almost, almost, so close.

choices.label: Reach one more inch.

nodes.body: Right then, a big gust of breeze swooped over the hill. The string spun loose off the pole, hopped right past Lila's fingers, and the big red balloon sailed up and away over the green treetops, smaller and smaller.

choices.label: Watch it go.

nodes.body: Lila's chin wobbled as the little red dot winked away behind the trees. The ice-cream man said a brave balloon chaser deserved a red treat, and handed her a strawberry cone. Grandpa hugged her close. The ice cream was sweet and cold, and next park day, they would pick a brand new balloon together.

At the windy top of the hill, the big red balloon rose in among the colorful kites, bobbing like a round red kite that had lost its tail. A kite kid named Jo grinned. "My yellow kite can help," she said.

choices.label: Ask Jo to try.

nodes.body: Jo let out more string, and her yellow kite swooped up right beside the big red balloon. Its long ribbon tail twirled gently around the balloon's string, soft as a hug, and held on tight.

choices.label: Reel them in together.

nodes.body: Hand over hand, Lila and Jo wound the reel together. Down came the yellow kite and the big red balloon, spinning slowly like falling leaves, lower and lower, until the string brushed against Lila's hands.

choices.label: Take hold of the string.

nodes.body: Lila held the big red balloon at last, and Jo took back her clever yellow kite. All the kite kids cheered from the hilltop. Grandpa tied the string with a double bow, and Lila and her brand new friend flew one more kite together before heading home.
